substeps.label: B6–B7 · cool, depowder, unload
substeps.caption: Cool and de-inert, depowder gently, photograph the plate in place, then lift the four inserts out. The plate only needs the powder blown out of the pocket gaps before the next run.

substeps.label: C1 · top-view images
substeps.caption: Each insert gets top-view images (are the tracks continuous, which ones balled up?). Insert A goes first, all the way through SEM, to catch problems early: track mapping, etch, SEM charging.

substeps.label: C2 · bandsaw: slab off
substeps.caption: Rough cut on the bandsaw (bi-metal blade, coolant for stainless): the insert goes on its side and the top 7 mm slab, which holds the tracks, comes off. The rest of the cube is discarded (option A).

substeps.label: C2 · bandsaw: one slab per row
substeps.caption: Then the slab lies flat and is split between the two rows: one slab per row of nine tracks. A bandsaw face is rough and deformed, so every bandsaw cut stays at least 1–2 mm from the target plane.

substeps.label: C2 · final face on the precision saw
substeps.caption: Final face on an abrasive cut-off saw or a low-speed precision saw with coolant (MIT used an IsoMet 4000 at 4000 rpm, 6 mm/min), 1.5 mm past the tracks' mid-length. Row 2 waits its turn.
